The Stoop isn't just an agency name — it's a philosophy. The best ideas don't come from boardrooms. They come from real conversations, real culture, and real people.

# Influencer Marketing — THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/services/influencer-marketing.html

## INFLUENCER MARKETING
Author: Mike Pernice , Founder · Last updated: July 2026
From strategy and influencer matching to execution, content approval, and ROI reporting — we manage every aspect of your influencer marketing program so you can focus on growing your brand.
### What's Included
- Influencer campaign strategy and planning
- Influencer sourcing, vetting, and matching
- Rate negotiation and contract management
- Content brief development and creative direction
- Deliverable tracking, approval workflows, and timelines
- Multi-platform execution (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook)
- Performance analytics and end-of-campaign reporting
- Multi-brand partnership brokering
Want influencer campaigns handled from sourcing to reporting?
### Who It's For
This service is built for brands in fitness, wellness, food & beverage, DTC, and apparel who want to scale through authentic influencer partnerships. Whether you're launching your first influencer campaign or looking to professionalize and scale an existing program, we handle the end-to-end workflow so your team can focus on product and growth.
### Influencers in Action
Creators we sourced, briefed, and activated · X Shadyside · Dr. Tea
Ashley Neicea reel
Cam Laconi reel
Ana Sofia reel
X Shadyside: the New Year, New Us cast
Reels from creators we sourced, briefed, and activated.
Want reach like this for your brand?
### See It in Action
See how influencer activation could work for you.
### Request a Proposal
Tell us about your brand and campaign goals. We'll get back to you within 24 hours.
### Frequently Asked Questions
#### How do you find and vet influencers?
We source influencers based on audience demographics, engagement rates, content quality, and brand alignment. Every influencer is vetted before activation — we review their content history, audience authenticity, and past brand partnerships.
#### What platforms do you run influencer campaigns on?
We primarily execute on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Facebook. Platform selection depends on your target audience and campaign goals.
#### How much does an influencer campaign cost?
Campaign budgets vary based on the number of influencers, deliverables, and usage rights. We've managed campaigns from $2,300 to $10,000+ in influencer spend alone, plus management fees.
#### How do you measure influencer campaign success?
We track views, impressions, engagements, link clicks, CPM, CPC, and conversion events. Every campaign ends with a detailed post-mortem report with actionable insights.
### Ready to put creators to work for your brand?
Let's build a campaign that drives real results.

# X Shadyside — Case Study | THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/work/x-shadyside.html

## X SHADYSIDE
Author: Mike Pernice , Founder · Last updated: September 2026
Two seasons of influencer-driven content campaigns and eight months of organic social for X Shadyside — a family-owned, all-inclusive fitness facility in Pittsburgh's Shadyside neighborhood, operating since 1994.
### "New Year, New Us"
30 Sourced · 7 Activated · December 2022 — February 2023
Ashley Neicea reel
Cam Laconi reel
Ana Sofia reel
Dr. Brian Meenan reel
Michelle Lagree reel
Miranda Martin reel
Group edit
Want a New Year membership push for your fitness brand?
### The Gym’s Own Feed, Week After Week
Instagram · Weekly Calendar · Promotions · Post-Level Analytics
After the New Year campaign, The Stoop took over X Shadyside’s own Instagram and ran it through the fall campaign and beyond. From May 15 to December 31, 2023, each month ran on a set package of about 24 stories, 8 reels, and 4 feed posts, planned week by week in a shared tracker that held every post’s topic, draft, and caption and, once it was live, its views, impressions, and engagements.
The calendar ran on recurring beats: Monday Motivation, reminders to get to the gym, member spotlights and client reviews, X Pump class promos, hours and location stories, polls and questions, and meet-the-owners posts. It carried the gym’s offers, from summer memberships and day passes to the refer-a-friend, $0 activation fee, and Fall into Fitness countdown, and it kept the Lucid Juice partnership in front of members with 21 posts and stories tagging the juice shop.
#### Reels Cut From the August Shoot
Group class on the blue turf
Bench day
Stair stepper
Straps, step-ups and lunges
Heavy bench, spotted
#### Promo Stories
#### From the August Content Shoot
Reels did the heavy lifting. Across the posts with Instagram analytics logged from June to December, reels averaged 929 views each, more than twice a feed post (417) and almost seven times a story (136). The top performer was a “Time Is Running Out” countdown reel for the Fall into Fitness offer at 4,183 views, followed by a gym-music reel at 2,771 and a November reel tagging Lucid Juice at 1,842. In every month with analytics logged, the account drew between 8,300 and 11,700 Instagram views.
Want a weekly calendar that keeps your gym’s feed full?
### "Fall into Fitness"
23 Sourced · 8 Activated · August — September 2023
Fall into Fitness paid ad reel
Need a back-to-school activation for your gym?
### X Shadyside × Lucid Juice
X Shadyside · SXP · Lucid Juice
The Stoop brokered a multi-brand partnership across X Shadyside, SXP, and Lucid Juice — resulting in custom-branded recovery juices, cross-promotional social, member discounts, and event sales.
Lucid Juice x X Shadyside reel
Want us to broker a multi-brand partnership for your business?
### Our Process
#### Sourcing
Sourced 50+ Pittsburgh-area fitness, lifestyle, and student-creator influencers across two seasons. Vetted for audience fit, engagement quality, and brand alignment.
#### Activation
Activated 15 influencers across two seasons under collaborative reel + story + likeness-rights deals. Onboarded each with brief, hashtags, and deliverable timelines.
#### Production
3-hour content shoots on location at the facility for each campaign. Produced reels, photos, story posts, and a paid ad reel with full brand framing.
#### Distribution & Reporting
Multi-platform posting (Instagram + Facebook), paid amplification, and full campaign reporting on views, engagements, link clicks, and CPM.
Team: Mike Pernice (Account Manager) · Jason Robinson (Multimedia Producer)
### Two Seasons of Measurable Reach
Influencer content consistently outperformed branded posts in engagement, the multi-brand partnership opened new revenue streams, and X Shadyside proved that local businesses with strong community roots can leverage influencer marketing to drive real, measurable growth.
Between and around the campaigns, the gym’s own Instagram logged 61K+ views over eight months of organic posting, with reels averaging 929 views each.
### Questions About This Project
**Q: What results did the X Shadyside influencer campaigns produce?**
Across two seasons, "New Year, New Us" in Q1 2023 and "Fall into Fitness" in Q3 2023, the campaigns generated 267K+ total views, 307K+ impressions, and 5.8K+ link clicks, with 15 influencers activated.
**Q: How many influencers took part?**
The Stoop sourced 30 influencers and activated 7 for the New Year campaign, then sourced 23 and activated 8 for Fall into Fitness, for 15 activated influencers in total.
**Q: What is the Lucid Juice partnership?**
The Stoop brokered a strategic partnership between X Shadyside, SXP, and Lucid Juice that added a member benefit and opened cross-promotion across the three Pittsburgh businesses.
**Q: Did The Stoop also run X Shadyside’s own social media?**
Yes. From May 15 to December 31, 2023, The Stoop ran X Shadyside’s Instagram on a monthly package of about 24 stories, 8 reels, and 4 feed posts, 254 pieces in all. More than 61,000 Instagram views were logged from June to December, and reels averaged 929 views each.
### Related Services
### Ready to build your next campaign?
Let's create something that moves your audience.

# Dr. Tea — Case Study | THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/work/dr-tea.html

## DR. TEA
Author: Mike Pernice , Founder · Last updated: September 2026
Dr. Tea is a family-owned bubble tea shop in Pittsburgh's Shadyside neighborhood. The Stoop ran the #LoveIsBrewing Valentine's Day influencer campaign — concept, local influencers, on-location shoots, and a digital ad — and paired it with a full-service marketing proposal to set the shop up for sustained growth.
### The Challenge
Dr. Tea was a beloved local bubble tea shop looking to amplify its brand presence and drive foot traffic — especially around key seasonal moments. As a small, family-owned business, they needed a marketing partner who could deliver big results on a lean budget.
The goal was clear: create buzz, build a loyal social following, and establish a scalable marketing foundation that could grow with the business.
### #LoveIsBrewing Influencer Campaign
Local Influencers · On-Location Content Shoots · Paid Digital Ad
A Valentine's Day campaign that turned Dr. Tea into a must-visit date spot, built on influencer content shot on location at the shop and a paid digital ad.
#LoveIsBrewing — Digital Ad
Emily & Mike — Influencer Content
Want a seasonal influencer campaign built around your brand's biggest moments?
### The Proposal
Beyond the campaign, The Stoop delivered a full-service marketing proposal that gave Dr. Tea a clear roadmap for brand identity, quarterly advertising, and ongoing influencer partnerships — positioning them for long-term growth.
- Brand identity
- Social media strategy and content calendar framework
- Quarterly ad campaigns
- Influencer marketing
Need a marketing roadmap before your next launch?
### Our Process
#### Campaign Concept
Built the #LoveIsBrewing concept and creative direction around one idea: Dr. Tea as the Valentine's Day date spot.
#### Influencer Sourcing
Sourced and managed local influencers for Valentine's Day content.
#### Content Production
Coordinated on-location content shoots at the shop and managed all influencer deliverables, timelines, and approvals.
#### Marketing Proposal
Delivered the full-service marketing proposal and content calendar framework so Dr. Tea could keep building after Valentine's Day.
### 480,334 Views From One Seasonal Campaign
The #LoveIsBrewing campaign exceeded expectations — generating 480,334 views, 651,244 impressions, 6,154 engagements, and 1,730 link clicks. The campaign drove 166 new followers during the promotion window, establishing Dr. Tea as a social media presence in Pittsburgh's food scene. Beyond the campaign, the full-service marketing proposal positioned Dr. Tea for long-term growth.
### Questions About This Project
**Q: How many views did the #LoveIsBrewing campaign get?**
The campaign generated 480,334 views, 651,244 impressions, 6,154 engagements, and 1,730 link clicks from one Valentine's Day campaign, and drove 166 new followers during the promotion window.
**Q: What did The Stoop do for Dr. Tea?**
Concept, local influencer sourcing, on-location content shoots, and a paid digital ad for the #LoveIsBrewing Valentine's Day launch, paired with a full-service marketing proposal for long-term growth.
**Q: Who is Dr. Tea?**
Dr. Tea is a family-owned bubble tea shop in Pittsburgh's Shadyside neighborhood.

### Our Process
#### Pre-Production
Master Services Agreement, shot list, location scouting, and influencer recruiting across two markets.
#### Production
Multi-day shoots across South Hills and Pearland. Cinematic video, photography, aerial drone, and on-site influencer activation.
#### Post-Production
Color grading, audio mixing, branding, text overlay, and multi-format delivery (9x16, 16x9, 1x1) for every channel.
#### Activation

# Take a Nurse — Case Study | THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/work/take-a-nurse.html

## TAKE A NURSE
Author: Mike Pernice , Founder · Last updated: September 2026
Take a Nurse is a nurse-driven, patient-focused small business in Pittsburgh, PA that advocates for independent individuals who need help understanding and navigating their medical care. The Stoop designed its visual identity from the mark up — a logo system built around a stethoscope that forms the N and resolves into a heart, five approved color variants, a seven-color palette, a two-typeface type system, business cards, letterhead, and a brand identity guide — and is now building the website on the same system.
### The Challenge
Take a Nurse grew out of founder Kathy Fadgen's own experience. Her out-of-town parents were going to medical appointments without her, and unknown treatment plans and medication changes led to stress, delayed care, and unnecessary emergency room visits. The brand had to feel like the service itself — a calm, trusted advocate — and it had to hold up everywhere a healthcare brand shows up: a website header, a business card, an embroidered uniform, a form, a phone screen. It also needed rules so it stays consistent no matter who produces the next piece. The Stoop delivered the full system: the mark, the lockups, the colors, the type, the stationery, and the guide that governs them.
### The Logo System
Horizontal Lockup · Stacked Lockup · Logomark · 5 Color Variants
The identity is built around one idea: a stethoscope that draws the N and resolves into a heart. The Stoop delivered it as three lockups — a horizontal default for websites, email headers, and signage; a stacked version for square formats and event graphics; and a standalone logomark for avatars, favicons, and watermarks — each supplied in Primary two-color, Blue, Magenta, Black, and White, with clear-space and minimum-size rules so the mark survives embroidery, vinyl, and small screens.
Need a mark that works on a business card and a building?
### Palette & Type System
Blue & Magenta Lead · Norteans Display · Roboto Text
Blue carries trust and structure; magenta carries energy and warmth. Care Teal, Warm Gold, Cloud, and Ink support them, each with a defined role and hex, RGB, and CMYK values so print and digital match. Norteans handles headlines and key numbers; Roboto does the reading, with a recommended scale from H1 to captions and a misuse page that protects proportion, color, spacing, and contrast.
Want a palette and type system your whole team can actually follow?
### Business Cards & Letterhead
Two-Sided Business Card · Letterhead · Print-Ready
The first pieces built on the system: a two-sided business card that puts the horizontal lockup and magenta accent on the front and the logomark, contact details, and Norteans name treatment on the back, plus a letterhead that carries the header and footer bar onto every printed page.
Need stationery that matches the brand you just built?
### Our Process
#### The Mark
Designed the stethoscope-and-heart N as the single idea the whole identity hangs on, then set the wordmark around it.
#### Lockups & Variants
Built horizontal, stacked, and logomark lockups and supplied each in five approved color variants, with clear-space and minimum-size floors.
#### Color & Type
Defined a seven-color palette with print and digital values, paired Norteans with Roboto, and set a recommended type scale.
#### Stationery & Guide
Produced print-ready business cards and letterhead, then documented everything in a nine-page brand identity guide.
### A System, Not Just a Logo
Pittsburgh, PA · August — September 2026 · Identity in Use · Website in Development
Take a Nurse now has one mark that scales from a favicon to signage, a palette and type pairing that match across print and screen, stationery ready for the printer, and a guide that lets anyone — a printer, an embroiderer, a web developer — produce on-brand work without rebuilding or guessing. The identity is in use, and The Stoop is now building the Take a Nurse website on the same system.
### Questions About This Project
**Q: What did The Stoop design for Take a Nurse?**
A logo system with horizontal, stacked, and logomark lockups in five color variants, a seven-color palette, a Norteans and Roboto type system, business cards, letterhead, and a nine-page brand identity guide.
**Q: Who is Take a Nurse?**
Take a Nurse is a nurse-driven, patient-focused small business in Pittsburgh, PA that advocates for independent individuals who need help understanding and navigating their medical care.
**Q: When was the work done?**
August to September 2026. The identity is in use, and The Stoop is now building the Take a Nurse website on the same system.

# Union Trust Building — Case Study | THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/work/union-trust-building.html

## UNION TRUST BUILDING
Social Media Management, Event Content & Tenant Communications
Author: Mike Pernice, Founder · Last updated: September 2026
The Union Trust Building is a Flemish Gothic landmark at 501 Grant Street in downtown Pittsburgh, redeveloped by The Davis Companies into Class-A offices with restaurants, a tenant gym, and a 10th-floor theatre. From October 2023 into 2025, The Stoop ran its Instagram and Facebook: tenant event coverage, a social media audit, and monthly reels and stories. We also produced the quarterly tenant newsletter and branded the building’s tenant app.
### The Challenge
The Union Trust Building has more to show than almost any office address in Pittsburgh: a 40-foot stained-glass dome, a 55-ton bank vault door installed in 1918, a Gothic roofline with chapels on top, and a lobby full of restaurants and tenants. Its social accounts mostly covered events. When we audited them in November 2023, they were reaching just 1.8% of the potential audience in the building’s top five cities, and had captured only 0.2% of it. The audience wanted more than events: the building itself, the people who run it, and the companies that work there.
Property management needed a partner who could do three things at once: cover tenant events the day they happen, keep a steady monthly calendar of reels and stories, and give tenants a reason to follow the building they work in.
### The Strategy
Our Social Media Analysis & Strategy compared almost two years of Facebook and Instagram data and set the plan for 2024:
- Lead with Instagram Reels, set to trending audio with on-screen text, where engagement was highest
- Reshare to Facebook with captions written for its older audience
- Widen the content beyond events: building history, behind-the-scenes tours, staff, and tenant spotlights
- Post stories consistently, with polls and Q&As to start conversations
- Use both accounts as an information hub for tenants: events, amenities, and building news
- Report quarterly on reach, interactions, and follower growth
### Events, Posted the Same Week
Happy Hours · Makers Markets · Taste of UTB · Trivia · Blood Drives · Quantum Theatre
The work started with tenant events. Each one came as a set package: one to two hours of on-site coverage, two reels, and five stories, with the first story posted live while the event was still going and the rest over the following days. From late 2024 every event ran on the same monthly cycle: an announcement, a content shoot, and a recap reel and story. Coverage ran from a Harvest Party in October 2023 through holiday happy hours, makers markets, a Taste of UTB tasting with five restaurants, and a Make-A-Wish fundraiser with BNY Mellon that passed its $5,000 goal halfway through and closed at more than $8,000.
Hosting events your audience should see?
### A Landmark With Recurring Series
December 2023 – March 2025 · Instagram · Facebook · Community Management
Monthly management began in December 2023 with a package of eight feed posts and eight stories a month, planned in a shared tracker and shot in regular content days around the building. The calendar ran on recurring series, so there was always a next episode: a six-part Day in the Life, History with Charles and Throwback Thursday posts on the building’s past, staff and tenant spotlights, restaurant collaborations, and building highlights from the dome to the art program.
#### The Building
#### Tenants, Staff & Series Templates
Want a monthly calendar built around your own story?
### Quarterly Tenant Newsletter
Fall 2024 · Winter 2025 · Spring 2025 · Event Recaps · Building News
From fall 2024 we also produced the building’s quarterly tenant newsletter, and it ran with the social calendar as one loop: each issue announced the coming season’s events, recapped the last season’s, and ran building features such as the restored chapel roof, the Pittsburgh History & Landmarks Foundation’s new vault panels, and the valet team. The recaps carried the outcomes tenants cared about: Quantum Theatre sold 2,101 tickets for its month-long run in the building’s theatre, and the March 2025 blood drive collected 19 donations, enough to help 57 local lives. Every issue sent readers back to the building’s Instagram and Facebook.
Need tenant or member communications that people read?
### The Building in Every Tenant’s Pocket
March 2025 · Login Screen · Splash Screen · App Icons · Notification Icon
In March 2025 we branded the building’s tenant app on the VTS platform: a login-screen background built from a photo of the stained-glass dome, login and splash-screen versions of the Union Trust Building logo, iOS and Android app icons, and an Android notification icon, each sized to the platform’s specs. Tenants who open the app see the same building they follow on Instagram.
Need a brand that holds up down to a phone icon?
### Our Process
#### Audit & Strategy
A full Facebook and Instagram audit comparing 2022 and 2023, an audience breakdown by age, interest, and city, and a 2024 plan with named goals and KPIs.
#### Event Packages
A fixed deliverable for every tenant event: on-site coverage, two reels, and five stories, with one story posted live and the rest scheduled over the following days.
#### Series & Shoot Days
Recurring series planned in a shared tracker, shot in content days around the building, with polls, Q&As, and tenant collabs built into the stories.
#### Quarterly Reporting
Per-post views, impressions, and engagement logged every month, and quarterly reports on reach, interactions, and follower growth for both platforms.
### More Reach, More Conversation
Instagram, the platform the strategy put first, moved fastest. In the first quarter of monthly management, Instagram content interactions went from 311 to 1,100 and Facebook interactions from 166 to 630. Quarterly Instagram reach climbed from 3,052 accounts in fall 2023 to 5,900 in Q1 2024 and 8,000 in Q2, and the account crossed 1,000 followers by the end of June 2024.
The series did the heavy lifting. Day in the Life Part 1 drew 2,155 Instagram views, the vault episode of History with Charles 2,000, and a staff spotlight on engineer Dan 2,500 views on Facebook, the most of any post there.
#### Quarter by Quarter
- Fall 2023 (Sep 29 – Dec 27) — 3,052 IG accounts reached, 311 IG interactions, 821 IG followers
- Q1 2024 — 5,900 IG accounts reached, 1,100 IG interactions, 910 IG followers
- Q1 2024 — 630 Facebook interactions, up from 166; Facebook followers 216 → 244
- Q2 2024 — 8,000 IG accounts reached, 1,004 IG followers
- Q2 2024 — 12,700 Facebook impressions, up from 12,100 in Q1
- Dec 2023 – Mar 2025 — 49,738 Instagram and 14,111 Facebook views logged across 219 posts and stories
The full year held up. In 2024, the first full year of monthly management, Instagram reached 16,600 accounts, up from 4,200 in 2023, and drew 24,100 views, up from 6,100. Content interactions rose from 255 to 1,000 on Instagram and from 218 to 1,500 on Facebook, where reach grew from 8,000 to 11,600 accounts. Instagram followers grew from 821 at the end of 2023 to 1,057 at the end of 2024, up 29%. The Stoop took over in October 2023, so the 2023 figures already include its first three months.
#### 2024 vs. 2023
- Instagram accounts reached — 4,200 → 16,600
- Instagram views — 6,100 → 24,100
- Instagram content interactions — 255 → 1,000
- Instagram profile visits — 1,100 → 2,900
- Facebook accounts reached — 8,000 → 11,600
- Facebook content interactions — 218 → 1,500
- Facebook page visits — 1,600 → 2,500
- Instagram followers — 821 → 1,057 (+29%)
- Facebook followers — 216 → 271 (+25%)
### Questions About This Project
**Q: What results did the Union Trust Building see?**
Instagram followers grew from 821 to 1,004 (+22%) between the end of 2023 and the end of Q2 2024, and quarterly Instagram reach grew from 3,052 to 8,000 accounts over the same span. Instagram content interactions rose from 311 to 1,100 quarter over quarter after monthly management began. Across all of 2024, compared with 2023, Instagram accounts reached grew from 4,200 to 16,600, Instagram views from 6,100 to 24,100, and Instagram followers from 821 to 1,057 (+29%).
**Q: What did the engagement include?**
Tenant event coverage with a set package of reels and stories per event, a social media audit and strategy, monthly Instagram and Facebook management with recurring video series, community management, quarterly analytics reporting, a quarterly tenant newsletter, and brand assets for the building’s tenant app.
**Q: What is the Union Trust Building?**
The Union Trust Building is a Flemish Gothic landmark at 501 Grant Street in downtown Pittsburgh, designed by Frederick Osterling for Henry Clay Frick and listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 1974. The Davis Companies redeveloped it as a Class-A historic office building in 2017.

# Michael Pernice, Founder — The Stoop, Pittsburgh
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/founder.html

## MICHAEL PERNICE
From a podcast platform for Pittsburgh creators to a full-service digital advertising and influencer marketing agency.
### How The Stoop Started
The Stoop launched in 2019 as a promotional platform and podcast for local athletes, businesses, creators, entrepreneurs, and organizations to increase their brand awareness in the Pittsburgh area.
The idea was simple. There were talented people doing incredible work in Pittsburgh and beyond who didn't have a platform or the marketing know-how to get noticed. The Stoop gave them one — a podcast, a social media presence, and a community. Across 48 episodes, The Stoop Podcast featured musicians, fitness professionals, nonprofit founders, filmmakers, dietitians, small business owners, and creatives from Pittsburgh, Cincinnati, Portland, Houston, and beyond.
The Stoop wasn't just a podcast — it was a movement. In August 2020, The Stoop organized the Legendz of The Stoop Virtual Benefit , a live-streamed charity event featuring local Pittsburgh comedians, musicians, artists, dancers, and a DJ. The event was produced in partnership with local businesses B-Sides Vintage and Follow The Trees Ride The Vibe, and raised over $1,000 for four Pittsburgh-area charities: One Hood, The Education Partnership, Beverley's Birthdays, and The Emma Munson Foundation.
That work — sitting down with creators, organizing community events, learning what local businesses and independent creators actually needed, and understanding the gap between talent and visibility — became the foundation for everything The Stoop is today.
What started as a microphone and a mission evolved into a full-service digital advertising and influencer marketing agency built at the intersection of culture, content, and commerce.
Legendz of The Stoop Virtual Benefit — live-streamed August 2020
### The Person Behind The Stoop
I built The Stoop because I saw a gap that nobody was filling.
Brands wanted influencer marketing but didn't know how to find the right influencers, manage campaigns, or measure what actually worked. Influencers and content creators wanted to turn their platforms into careers but had no one teaching them how to pitch, price, or negotiate. Both sides were figuring it out alone — and both sides were leaving money and opportunity on the table.
The Stoop exists to bridge that gap. We help brands scale through authentic influencer partnerships. We coach influencers to build sustainable businesses through our influencer coaching program. And we deliver the full spectrum of digital advertising services that make it all work — from paid media and organic social to content production and marketing automation .
Want to talk through your brand's next move with Mike directly?

### Why a Collective — Not a Traditional Agency
Most digital advertising agencies hire generalists and stretch them across every account. The Stoop doesn't work that way.
We operate as a collective — a curated network of experienced account managers, specialized freelancers, and exclusive agency partners who each bring deep expertise in their discipline. When a brand works with The Stoop, they get a social media strategist who lives and breathes organic content, an influencer marketing specialist who has sourced and managed hundreds of influencer relationships, a videographer with professional cinema equipment, and a paid media buyer who optimizes campaigns daily — not one person trying to do all four.
Our partnerships with Responsival and Blink Advertising extend our capabilities into web development , SEO, and traditional media buying without adding overhead or diluting our focus.
It's the reason we can deliver 81 production assets for $4,000 , generate 480K views for a local business on a $4 CPM , or raise $47,000 for a nonprofit at 87% below the industry cost-per-click benchmark . The collective model isn't a workaround. It's an advantage.

# How We Work — Our 4-Step Marketing Process | THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/process.html

## FROM CONVERSATION TO RESULTS
Author: Mike Pernice , Founder
Every engagement follows the same 4-step framework. Whether it's a single influencer campaign or a full-year marketing program, the structure stays consistent. It's how we deliver predictable results without surprises.
### DISCOVERY
We start by listening. Every project begins with a free consultation where we learn your business, your goals, your audience, and your budget. No pitch deck. No sales pressure. Just a real conversation about what you need.
- What happens: 30–60 minute call or meeting
- We learn: Your business model, target audience, competitors, past marketing efforts, and budget
- You learn: Whether we're the right fit, what services apply, and what results are realistic
- Deliverable: Custom proposal with scope, timeline, and pricing within 48 hours
### STRATEGY
Once we're aligned, we build the blueprint. This is the most important step — strategy determines whether your budget works hard or gets wasted. We don't skip this for any engagement, no matter how small.
- What happens: Deep-dive research into your market, audience, and platform data
- For influencer campaigns: Influencer sourcing, vetting, rate negotiation, and content brief development
- For paid media: Audience architecture, platform selection, creative concepts, and budget allocation
- For organic social: Content pillar development, posting calendar, hashtag strategy, and competitor analysis
- Deliverable: Strategy document + content calendar, signed off before any execution begins
### EXECUTION
We do the work. Production, posting, campaign management, optimization — all handled by our team. You stay in the loop with regular check-ins but don't need to manage the day-to-day.
- Content production: Professional shoots with cinema-grade gear (Sony FX3, drones, lighting)
- Influencer management: Contract execution, content approval workflows, posting coordination
- Paid media: Campaign launch, A/B testing, real-time optimization, budget pacing
- Organic social: Daily posting, community management, engagement, and story content
- Client touchpoint: Weekly or bi-weekly syncs depending on engagement scope
### REPORTING
Every dollar gets accounted for. We deliver detailed analytics showing exactly what your investment produced — benchmarked against industry standards so you know if your results are good, great, or exceptional.
- Metrics tracked: Views, impressions, engagements, link clicks, CPM, CPC, CTR, conversions, ROI
- Benchmarking: Your results compared against industry averages so performance has context
- Actionable insights: What worked, what didn't, and what to do next
- Deliverable: End-of-campaign report (projects) or monthly analytics report (retainers)
- What's next: Strategy recommendations for the next phase based on real data
### What Makes Us Different
- No work starts without a signed strategy. We never wing it. Every campaign has a plan before a single dollar is spent or a single post goes live
- We use real data, not vibes. Every recommendation is backed by platform analytics, campaign benchmarks, and audience data
- You own everything we create. Content, strategies, reports — it's all yours once paid for. No hostage situations
- We're small on purpose. You work directly with the founder and senior team, not junior account managers
- Transparent pricing, transparent reporting. No hidden fees, no inflated metrics. See our pricing page for ranges
### Ready to Start?
Step 1 is free. Fill out a proposal request and we'll set up a discovery call within 24 hours.
No commitment. No pressure. Just a conversation about what you need.

# FAQ — Influencer Marketing, Pricing & Process | THE STOOP
Source: https://thestooppgh.com/faq.html

## EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW
Last updated: July 2026 · Author: Mike Pernice , Founder
### General
#### What is The Stoop?
The Stoop is a Pittsburgh-based digital advertising and influencer marketing agency founded in 2019. We help brands scale through influencer partnerships, paid media campaigns, and content production. We also coach influencers to build sustainable careers. Our clients span fitness, food & beverage, healthcare, nonprofits, landscaping, and sports performance.
#### What services does The Stoop offer?
We offer 8 core services: Influencer Marketing, Digital Advertising, Organic Social Media Management, Content Development, Marketing Automation & Ops, Design & Branding, Website Design & Development, and Influencer Coaching. Each service can be engaged individually or bundled into a comprehensive marketing program.
#### Where is The Stoop located?
We're based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. We serve local Pittsburgh businesses as well as national clients. Contact us at mike@thestooppgh.com or call (412) 616-0542.
#### What industries do you specialize in?
We go deep in fitness & wellness, food & beverage, healthcare & medical, nonprofit organizations, landscaping & home services, sports performance, and local retail. Our case studies include X Shadyside (fitness), Dr. Tea (bubble tea), MFPAA (nonprofit EMS), Sylvan Gardens (landscaping), Iron 24 (gym franchise), SXP (sports performance), and Case Specific Meal Prep (food).
#### Do you work with small businesses?
Yes. Most of our clients are small to mid-size businesses in the Pittsburgh area. We've worked with single-location restaurants, local fitness studios, landscaping companies, meal prep services, and nonprofit organizations. We don't have minimum spend requirements — we build programs that fit your budget.
### Influencer Marketing
#### How much does influencer marketing cost?
Influencer marketing campaigns typically range from $2,000 to $15,000+ depending on the number of influencers, content deliverables, usage rights, and campaign duration. Micro-influencer activations (1K–25K followers) typically cost $100–$1,000 per influencer. Mid-tier (25K–100K) typically cost $500–$3,500. Our average cost per view across campaigns is $0.025.
#### How do you find and vet influencers?
We source influencers based on audience demographics, engagement rates, content quality, geographic relevance, and brand alignment. Every influencer is vetted before activation — we review content history, audience authenticity, past brand partnerships, and check for non-compete conflicts. For X Shadyside, we sourced 23 influencers to lock in 8 for Campaign 2.
#### What does an influencer campaign include?
A typical campaign includes: strategy development, influencer sourcing & vetting, contract negotiation, creative direction, on-site content shoot coordination, content approval workflow, posting schedule management, performance tracking, and end-of-campaign analytics reporting. We manage the entire process end-to-end.
### Digital Advertising
#### How much does digital advertising cost?
Management fees typically range from $1,500 to $5,000 per month plus your ad spend budget. We work across Meta (Facebook & Instagram), LinkedIn, Google Ads, and YouTube. Our MFPAA nonprofit campaign delivered a $1.56 CPC — 87% below the $3.97 industry benchmark — on a $3,645 media budget.
#### How do you measure campaign success?
We track CPM (cost per thousand impressions), CPC (cost per click), CTR (click-through rate), engagement rate, link clicks, conversions, and ROI. Every campaign includes detailed analytics reporting benchmarked against industry standards so you can see exactly how your investment performed.
### Organic Social Media
#### How much does organic social media management cost?
Organic social management typically ranges from $1,500 to $5,000 per month depending on the number of platforms, posting frequency, content production needs, and community management scope. This includes strategy, content creation, scheduling, engagement, and monthly analytics reporting.
#### How long does it take to see results from organic social?
Organic social is a long game. Expect 3–6 months of consistent posting to build meaningful momentum. For Sylvan Gardens, we drove 38K+ total impact in the first 9 months, then 181 net new followers over the first full year, more than four times the year before — all with zero ad spend. The compound effect of consistent, quality content is the value proposition.
### Content Development
#### How much does content production cost?
Content production ranges from $1,500 to $10,000+ per project depending on scope. A gym tour video package (1 video + 10 reels + 30 photos) runs approximately $1,775. A comprehensive production (20 videos + 60 photos + 1 drone video) runs approximately $4,000. We use professional cinema cameras (Sony FX3), lighting, stabilizers, and drones.
### Influencer Coaching
#### What is influencer coaching?
Influencer coaching is our 1-on-1 program that teaches influencers how to pitch brands, negotiate rates, build media kits, develop personal branding, create rate strategies, and turn content creation into a sustainable career. It's for influencers who are ready to treat their platform as a business.
### Process & Working Together
#### Do you require long-term contracts?
It depends on the service. Influencer campaigns are project-based with no long-term commitment. Organic social management and digital advertising typically operate on monthly retainers with 30–90 day termination clauses. We use formal Master Services Agreements (MSAs) and Statements of Work (SOWs) for all engagements.
#### Can you help with nonprofit marketing?
Yes. We manage paid media and comprehensive marketing strategy for McCandless-Franklin Park Ambulance Authority (MFPAA), a nonprofit 501(c)(3) EMS provider serving McCandless, Franklin Park, Marshall, Pine, and Bradford Woods. Our capital campaign raised $47,139 from 446 donors in 30 days.
#### How do I get started?
Fill out a proposal request on any of our service pages or email mike@thestooppgh.com directly. We respond within 24 hours with next steps. No commitment required to start the conversation.
Still have questions? We're happy to chat.
